heading: Income and deductions
summary: Top-level section governing what counts as income, what is excluded, and what deductions apply when determining SNAP eligibility and benefit level.

heading: Income eligibility standards
summary: Establishes gross- and net-income tests as a precondition for participation. Households with elderly/disabled members must meet only net; other households must meet both gross and net; categorically eligible households are exempt from both.
key_quote: "Households which contain an elderly or disabled member shall meet the net income eligibility standards for SNAP."

heading: Gross income eligibility standards
summary: Gross income limit is set at 130% of the Federal poverty level, with separate scales for the 48 contiguous states/DC/Guam/USVI, Alaska, and Hawaii.
key_quote: "shall be 130 percent of the Federal income poverty levels"

heading: Gross income standard, 48 states / DC / Guam / USVI
summary: 130% of the federal poverty guidelines for the 48 states and DC applies to those jurisdictions plus Guam and the Virgin Islands.

heading: Gross income standard, Alaska
summary: 130% of the Alaska federal poverty levels applies in Alaska.

heading: Gross income standard, Hawaii
summary: 130% of the Hawaii federal poverty levels applies in Hawaii.

heading: Net income eligibility standards
summary: Net income limit equals the Federal poverty guidelines, set separately for the 48 contiguous states/DC/Guam/USVI, Alaska, and Hawaii.
key_quote: "shall be the Federal income poverty levels"

heading: Annual October 1 update of income limits
summary: Both gross and net income standards are revised every October 1 to reflect annual updates to the federal poverty guidelines, with monthly amounts derived by dividing the annual figure by 12 and rounding up.
key_quote: "are revised each October 1"

heading: Publication of monthly income standards
summary: The monthly gross and net income standards are published in tables on the FNS web site rather than in the regulation itself.

heading: Definition of income
summary: Household income means all income from whatever source, excluding only the items specifically listed as exclusions in 273.9(c). This is the master inclusion rule.
key_quote: "Household income shall mean all income from whatever source excluding only items specified in paragraph (c) of this section."

heading: Earned income (umbrella)
summary: Defines the categories of receipts that count as earned income (wages, self-employment, training allowances, certain volunteer pay, on-the-job training under WIA, and work-study above exclusion threshold).

heading: Wages and salaries of employees
summary: All wages and salaries paid to an employee are earned income. Civica's W-2/paystub workers map directly to this clause.
household_types_affected: tipped workers, cash-paid workers, all earned-income households
key_quote: "All wages and salaries of an employee."

heading: Gross self-employment income; rental as self-employment; boarders
summary: Gross income from a self-employment enterprise (less costs of producing income per 273.9(c)) counts as earned income. Rental income is self-employment only if a household member actively manages it at least 20 hours/week. Boarder payments (other than foster boarders) count as self-employment income.
key_quote: "The gross income from a self-employment enterprise, including the total gain from the sale of any capital goods or equipment related to the business, excluding the costs of doing business"

heading: Training allowances from vocational/rehab programs
summary: Vocational and rehabilitative training allowances recognized by federal/state/local governments are earned income to the extent they are not a reimbursement. WIA training allowances other than (b)(1)(v) earnings are excluded.

heading: VISTA / Title I Domestic Volunteer Service Act payments
summary: Title I (VISTA, etc.) payments are earned income subject to the 20% earned income deduction, except for the households described in 273.9(c)(10)(iii).

heading: On-the-job training under WIA Title I
summary: Earnings from WIA Title I on-the-job training are earned income; this does NOT apply to household members under age 19 under the parental control of another adult member.

heading: Educational assistance with a work requirement (above exclusion)
summary: Work-study, assistantships, and fellowships with a work requirement count as earned income to the extent they exceed the 273.9(c)(3) exclusion. Higher Education Act 1087uu work-study is excluded entirely.

heading: Unearned income (umbrella)
summary: Non-exhaustive list of unearned income types -- assistance payments, pensions, support/alimony from outside the household, scholarships above exclusion, dividends and interest, and trust withdrawals.
key_quote: "Unearned income shall include, but not be limited to"

heading: Public assistance payments as unearned income
summary: SSI, TANF, state/local GA, and other need-based assistance count as unearned income, including when paid as vendor payments (unless specifically excluded under 273.9(c)(1)). Workfare-type payments conditioned on uncompensated work are also unearned income.

heading: Annuities, pensions, retirement, UI, worker's comp, foster care, passive rental
summary: Annuities, pensions, retirement benefits, veterans' or disability benefits, worker's or unemployment compensation, social security, strike benefits, foster-care payments for in-household members, and net rental income from property where the household does not actively manage 20+ hr/wk.

heading: Support or alimony from nonhousehold members
summary: Support or alimony paid directly to the household from a nonhousehold member counts as unearned income.

heading: Scholarships and educational grants above exclusion
summary: Scholarships, grants, deferred education loans, and veterans' educational benefits in excess of the 273.9(c) exclusions count as unearned income.

heading: Government-sponsored payments, dividends, interest, royalties
summary: Government-sponsored program payments plus dividends, interest, royalties, and any direct money payments construable as a gain count as unearned income. Catch-all for passive income streams.
key_quote: "all other direct money payments from any source which can be construed to be a gain or benefit"

heading: Trust fund withdrawals and dividends
summary: Money withdrawn from (or dividends receivable from) excludable trust funds under 273.8(e)(8) is unearned income in the month received unless otherwise exempt under 273.9(c).

heading: Income of disqualified or sanctioned members
summary: Income of a member disqualified for intentional program violation or workfare noncompliance is fully attributed to remaining members. Income of members disqualified for SSN noncompliance or ineligible alien status is counted minus a pro rata share for the disqualified member.

heading: Sponsor deeming for sponsored aliens
summary: For sponsored-alien households, sponsor and sponsor-spouse income is deemed in accordance with 273.4(c)(2).

heading: Items that do NOT count as income
summary: Money withheld or returned to repay a prior overpayment from the same income source is not counted as income (unless excluded under 273.9(c)). TANF-recipient child support that must be assigned to the IV-D agency is not counted.

heading: Overpayment recoupment from same source
summary: Money withheld or returned to repay a prior overpayment from the same income source is not income, provided the original overpayment was not itself excludable.

heading: Child support assigned to IV-D agency
summary: Child support that TANF recipients must transfer to the IV-D agency to maintain TANF eligibility is not counted as income.

heading: Income exclusions (closed list)
summary: Establishes the closed list of income exclusions -- no exclusions are permitted beyond those enumerated here. This is the master exclusion rule.
key_quote: "Only the following items shall be excluded from household income and no other income shall be excluded"

heading: In-kind benefits and certain vendor payments
summary: Non-monetary gains (in-kind benefits such as meals, clothing, housing, garden produce) are excluded. Vendor payments (paid to a third party on the household's behalf) are excluded or counted depending on the rules in (c)(1)(i)-(vii).

heading: Public assistance (PA) vendor payments
summary: PA vendor payments are counted as income unless they are for medical assistance, child care, energy assistance, migrant emergency assistance, housing-authority assistance, or qualifying emergency/special assistance.

heading: Medical-assistance vendor payments excluded
summary: PA vendor payments for medical assistance are excluded from income.

heading: Child-care vendor payments excluded
summary: PA vendor payments for child care assistance are excluded from income.

heading: Energy assistance vendor payments excluded
summary: PA vendor payments for energy assistance (as defined in 273.9(c)(11)) are excluded from income.

heading: Migrant/seasonal farmworker emergency assistance vendor payments excluded
summary: PA emergency assistance -- including housing and transportation -- paid to a third party for migrant or seasonal farmworker households while in the job stream is excluded.

heading: Housing-authority assistance excluded
summary: Housing assistance payments made through a State or local housing authority are excluded from income.

heading: Emergency and special assistance (vendor) excluded
summary: PA vendor payments that are over-and-above the normal grant -- emergencies, one-off special needs -- are excluded; State agencies must apply to FNS Regional Office when classification is unclear.

heading: General assistance (GA) vendor payments
summary: GA vendor payments are excluded from income except for housing-related GA, which is counted unless it falls into one of the five carve-outs (energy, housing-authority, migrant emergency, emergency/special, or no-cash-GA states).

heading: HUD vendor payments (rent / mortgage)
summary: Rent or mortgage payments made by HUD directly to landlords or mortgagees are excluded from income.

heading: Educational assistance vendor payments
summary: Educational assistance paid to a third party for the household's living expenses is treated the same as if paid directly to the household.

heading: Vendor reimbursements
summary: Reimbursements made as vendor payments are excluded on the same basis as cash reimbursements under 273.9(c)(5).

heading: Demonstration project vendor-to-cash conversions
summary: In-kind or vendor payments converted to direct cash payments under an authorized federal demonstration or waiver are excluded from income.

heading: Other third-party payments; wage garnishment treatment
summary: Money legally owed to the household but diverted by the payer to a third party counts as income; money the payer pays to a third party that was never owed to the household is excluded. Critical for garnishment, voluntary court-ordered direct-pay support, and friend/relative rent payments.
household_types_affected: all earned-income households, gig/contract workers, tipped workers, cash-paid workers
key_quote: "moneys legally obligated and otherwise payable to the household which are diverted by the provider of the payment to a third party for a household expense shall be counted as income"

heading: Infrequent or irregular income (de minimis)
summary: Income received too infrequently or irregularly to be reasonably anticipated is excluded, but not more than $30 per quarter.
household_types_affected: gig/contract workers, tipped workers, cash-paid workers
key_quote: "received too infrequently or irregularly to be reasonably anticipated, but not in excess of $30 in a quarter"

heading: Educational assistance exclusion (umbrella)
summary: Grants, scholarships, fellowships, work-study, deferred educational loans, and veterans' educational benefits are excluded if they meet the conditions in (c)(3)(ii)-(iv).

heading: Categories of excludable educational assistance
summary: Identifies the categories of educational assistance eligible for exclusion: grants, scholarships, fellowships, work-study, deferred-payment educational loans, veterans' educational benefits, and the like.

heading: Conditions for educational exclusion (source, school type, earmarked use)
summary: To be excluded, educational assistance must be (A) received under specified federal authorities or (B) awarded to a student at a qualifying post-secondary or vocational institution, and (C) earmarked for tuition, fees, books, supplies, transportation, miscellaneous personal expenses, dependent care, or origination fees/insurance -- not room and board.

heading: Timing of educational exclusions
summary: Educational exclusions are tied to the period the educational income is intended to cover, regardless of when actually received. Unearned educational income is exhausted first before earned educational income.

heading: Cap on educational exclusion per individual
summary: Total educational exclusions for an individual cannot exceed that individual's total qualifying educational income.

heading: State option: align educational exclusions with State Medicaid
summary: State agency option: exclude additional educational assistance that must be excluded under State Medicaid rules. State must elect this in its State Plan of Operation. STATE-OPTION JOIN.
key_quote: "At its option, the State agency may exclude any educational assistance that must be excluded under its State Medicaid rules"

heading: Loans excluded
summary: All loans -- private or commercial -- are excluded from income. Repayment must begin more than 60 days after receipt for a loan to qualify as deferred.
key_quote: "All loans, including loans from private individuals as well as commercial institutions"

heading: Reimbursements for past or future expenses
summary: Reimbursements (cash or flat allowance) for an identified expense other than normal living expenses are excluded to the extent they do not exceed actual expenses. Reimbursements for normal living expenses (rent, food at home, personal clothing) are NOT excluded.
key_quote: "Reimbursements for past or future expenses, to the extent they do not exceed actual expenses, and do not represent a gain or benefit to the household"

heading: Job/training travel and per diem reimbursements
summary: Reimbursements (or flat allowances) for job- or training-related travel, per diem, uniforms, and transportation are excluded. Migrant workers' travel reimbursements are also excluded. Civica relevance: rideshare/delivery worker per-mile reimbursements may attach here.
key_quote: "Reimbursements or flat allowances ... for job- or training-related expenses such as travel, per diem, uniforms, and transportation"

heading: Volunteer out-of-pocket reimbursements
summary: Reimbursements to volunteers for out-of-pocket expenses incurred in the course of volunteer work are excluded.

heading: Medical / dependent care reimbursements
summary: Medical or dependent-care reimbursements are excluded from income.

heading: Title XX SSA reimbursements
summary: Reimbursements received by households to pay for services provided by Title XX of the Social Security Act are excluded.

heading: School clothing allowance
summary: An annual school-clothing allowance for children entering or returning to school/daycare is excluded, provided the State agency does not reduce the month's TANF payment.

heading: E&T participation expense reimbursements
summary: Reimbursements made under 273.7(d)(3) for expenses necessary for participation in an E&T education component are excluded.

heading: Items NOT excludable as reimbursements
summary: Title IV-A SSA portions attributable to work-related or child-care adjustments, and educational assistance for normal living expenses (room and board), are NOT excludable as reimbursements.

heading: Care and maintenance of a third-party nonhousehold beneficiary
summary: Money used for the care and maintenance of a third-party beneficiary who is not a household member is excluded. Mixed-beneficiary payments are prorated when the nonhousehold portion is not identifiable.

heading: Earned income of minors in school
summary: Earned income of household members under 18 who are elementary or secondary school students (including GED, home-school) and who live with a parent or under parental control is excluded. Includes temporary breaks in school attendance.
key_quote: "The earned income ... of any household member who is under age 18, who is an elementary or secondary school student"

heading: Nonrecurring lump-sum payments
summary: Nonrecurring lump-sum payments -- tax refunds, retroactive SSI/SS/RR benefits, insurance settlements, security-deposit refunds, TANF diversion payments -- are excluded from income; they are counted as resources beginning the month received.
key_quote: "Money received in the form of a nonrecurring lump-sum payment"

heading: Cost of producing self-employment income
summary: The cost of producing self-employment income is excluded from income. Computation procedures are in 273.11. This is the central authority for Civica's gig/self-employment net-income calculations.
key_quote: "The cost of producing self-employment income."

heading: Federal statutory income exclusions (umbrella)
summary: Income that any other federal statute mandates be excluded from SNAP eligibility determinations. Subsections (i)-(x) enumerate the specific federal laws.

heading: Uniform Relocation Act reimbursements
summary: Reimbursements under the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policy Act of 1970 are excluded.

heading: Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act payments
summary: Payments under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act are excluded.

heading: Title II Domestic Volunteer Service Act / VISTA
summary: Title II Domestic Volunteer Service Act payments (RSVP, Foster Grandparents, etc.) are excluded. Title I (VISTA, UYA) payments are excluded only for participants who were receiving SNAP or PA when they joined the program; otherwise treated as earned income.

heading: Indian submarginal-land trust income
summary: Income from certain submarginal land held in trust for Indian tribes is excluded.

heading: WIA 1998 payments
summary: Payments and reimbursements to participants in Workforce Investment Act programs are excluded, except those provided for in 273.9(b)(1)(v).

heading: Grand River Band of Ottawa Indians
summary: Income from disposition of funds to the Grand River Band of Ottawa Indians is excluded.

heading: Pre-1980 EITC (historical)
summary: EITC payments received before January 1, 1980 (per Pub. L. 95-600) are excluded -- historical provision.

heading: Indian Claims Commission payments (Yakima / Mescalero)
summary: Indian Claims Commission payments to the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakima Indian Nation and the Apache Tribe of the Mescalero Reservation are excluded.

heading: Maine Indian Claims Settlement payments
summary: Payments to the Passamaquoddy Tribe and the Penobscot Nation under the Maine Indian Claims Settlement Act of 1980 are excluded.

heading: Navajo/Hopi relocation assistance
summary: Relocation assistance payments to members of the Navajo and Hopi Tribes under Pub. L. 93-531 are excluded.

heading: Energy assistance
summary: Energy-assistance payments and weatherization/emergency furnace repair payments are excluded.

heading: Federal energy assistance payments
summary: Federal energy-assistance payments (including HUD and Rural Housing Service utility reimbursements) are excluded -- but not Title IV-A SSA payments.

heading: One-time weatherization / emergency heating payment
summary: A one-time, as-needed payment under federal or state law for weatherization or emergency repair/replacement of an unsafe or inoperative heating or cooling device is excluded.

heading: Cash charitable donations under $300/quarter
summary: Cash donations based on need from one or more private nonprofit charities, not to exceed $300 in a federal fiscal-year quarter, are excluded.
key_quote: "Cash donations based on need ... but not to exceed $300 in a Federal fiscal year quarter"

heading: Earned Income Tax Credit payments
summary: EITC payments -- whether lump sum or advance under 3507 IRC -- are excluded from income.
household_types_affected: all earned-income households, tipped workers, gig/contract workers
key_quote: "Earned income tax credit payments received either as a lump sum or payments under section 3507 of the Internal Revenue Code"

heading: E&T participant cost payments
summary: Payments to E&T participants under 273.7(d)(3) for reasonably necessary costs (dependent care, transportation, uniforms, books, etc.) are excluded. Meals away from home are not included.

heading: Governmental foster care payments (boarder treatment)
summary: Governmental foster-care payments are excluded from income when the foster individual is treated as a boarder per 273.1(c).

heading: SSI PASS plan income
summary: Income of an SSI recipient necessary for a PASS (Plan for Achieving Self-Support) approved under SSA is excluded.

heading: Legally obligated child support paid out
summary: Legally obligated child support payments paid by a household member to or for a nonhousehold member (including third-party vendor payments and arrears) are excluded from income. State agencies may opt to provide a deduction under 273.9(d)(5) instead. STATE-OPTION JOIN.
key_quote: "Legally obligated child support payments paid by a household member to or for a nonhousehold member"

heading: State option: complementary assistance program payments
summary: State agency option: exclude State complementary assistance program payments that are excluded for Medicaid 1931 purposes. STATE-OPTION JOIN.

heading: State option: TANF/Medicaid-aligned income exclusions
summary: State agency option: exclude types of income that the State excludes when determining TANF or Medicaid 1931 eligibility, but only for the same amount. Wages, self-employment income, SSA benefits (Title I/II/IV/X/XIV/XVI), government payments, workers' comp, child support, alimony, pensions, disability/survivor benefits, and excludable-trust withdrawals may NOT be excluded under this option. STATE-OPTION JOIN.
key_quote: "At the State agency option, any types of income that the State agency excludes when determining eligibility or benefits for TANF cash assistance"

heading: Wages/salaries cannot be excluded under TANF/Medicaid alignment option
summary: Wages and salaries cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option.

heading: Self-employment cannot be excluded under TANF/Medicaid alignment option
summary: Gross self-employment income (including types referenced in 273.9(b)(1)(ii)) cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option. Self-employment monthly income must be calculated per 273.11(a)(2).
key_quote: "Determining monthly income from self-employment must be calculated in accordance with 273.11(a)(2)"

heading: SSA Title I/II/IV/X/XIV/XVI benefits cannot be excluded
summary: SSI, TANF, foster care, adoption payments from government sources cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option.

heading: Regular government payments cannot be excluded
summary: Regular payments from a government source -- including intermediary payments funded from a government source -- cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option.

heading: Worker's comp cannot be excluded
summary: Worker's compensation cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option.

heading: Child support / alimony from nonhousehold members cannot be excluded
summary: Child support and support/alimony from nonhousehold members cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option.

heading: Annuities / pensions / retirement cannot be excluded
summary: Annuities, pensions, and retirement benefits cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option.

heading: Disability / OASI cannot be excluded
summary: Disability benefits and old-age or survivor benefits cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option.

heading: Excludable-trust withdrawals cannot be re-excluded
summary: Money withdrawn from excludable-resource trust funds (273.8(e)(8)) cannot be excluded under the 273.9(c)(19) State option.

heading: Combat-zone military pay supplements
summary: Income received by U.S. Armed Forces members under Chapter 5 of Title 37 USC is excluded if it is (i) above basic pay, (ii) tied to deployment/service in a designated combat zone, and (iii) not received before deployment.
key_quote: "Received as a result of the service member deployment to or service in an area designated as a combat zone"

heading: Income deductions
summary: Establishes the closed list of allowable deductions: standard deduction, earned income deduction, excess medical, dependent care, optional child support, and shelter (including homeless shelter deduction and excess shelter).
key_quote: "Deductions shall be allowed only for the following household expenses"

heading: Standard deduction (umbrella)
summary: Standard deduction subtracted from gross income for every eligible household, with size- and jurisdiction-specific amounts and an annual CPI-indexed floor.

heading: Standard deduction -- 48 states, DC, Alaska, Hawaii, USVI
summary: Standard deduction equals 8.31% of the monthly net income eligibility standard, by household size 1-6 (capped at the size-6 amount for larger households), rounded up to whole dollars.
key_quote: "8.31 percent of the monthly net income eligibility standard"

heading: Standard deduction -- Guam
summary: Guam's standard deduction is 8.31% of double the 48-state monthly net income standard for sizes 1-6, capped at size 6.

heading: Minimum standard deduction floor
summary: Standard deduction may not fall below FY 2009 floors of $144 / $246 / $203 / $289 / $127 for 48 states / Alaska / Hawaii / Guam / USVI respectively; thereafter adjusted annually for non-food CPI.

heading: Earned income deduction -- 20%
summary: Twenty percent of gross earned income is deducted. Excluded earnings under 273.9(c) are not included in the deduction base, except that earnings used to pay child support excluded under 273.9(c)(17) ARE included in the deduction base.
household_types_affected: all earned-income households, tipped workers, gig/contract workers
key_quote: "Twenty percent of gross earned income"

heading: Excess medical deduction (elderly/disabled)
summary: For elderly or disabled household members (per 271.2), medical expenses above $35/month are deductible. Spouses or dependents receiving SSI benefits are not eligible; presumptive-eligibility SSI recipients are.
key_quote: "That portion of medical expenses in excess of $35 per month, excluding special diets, incurred by any household member who is elderly or disabled"

heading: Medical and dental care
summary: Medical and dental care -- including psychotherapy and rehabilitation services from licensed practitioners -- is a deductible medical expense.

heading: Hospitalization and nursing care
summary: Hospitalization, outpatient treatment, nursing care, and nursing home care (including payment for a former household member) are deductible.

heading: Prescription drugs and OTC medication
summary: Prescription drugs, plus OTC medications (including insulin) when approved by a licensed practitioner or qualified health professional, are deductible. Schedule I substances are not deductible.

heading: Health insurance premiums
summary: Health and hospitalization insurance premiums are deductible. Death/dismemberment lump-sum policies and disability-income policies are not deductible.

heading: Medicare premiums and Medicaid cost-sharing
summary: Medicare Title XVIII premiums and any Medicaid cost-sharing or spend-down expenses are deductible.

heading: Dentures, hearing aids, prosthetics
summary: Dentures, hearing aids, and prosthetics are deductible.

heading: Service animals
summary: Securing and maintaining a seeing-eye or hearing dog -- including dog food and veterinary bills -- is deductible.

heading: Prescription eyeglasses
summary: Eyeglasses prescribed by a physician or optometrist are deductible.

heading: Medical transportation and lodging
summary: Reasonable transportation and lodging costs to obtain medical treatment are deductible.

heading: Attendant care / home health aide
summary: Costs of maintaining an attendant, homemaker, home health aide, child-care services, or housekeeper necessary due to age, infirmity, or illness are deductible, plus a one-person-allotment-equivalent meal deduction if the household furnishes most of the attendant's meals. Attendant-care costs cannot be deducted under both medical and dependent care.

heading: Dependent care deduction
summary: Dependent care payments are deductible when necessary for a member to seek/accept/continue employment, comply with E&T requirements, or attend training/education preparatory to employment. Covers children under 18 or incapacitated adults; relative-provided care is allowed if the relative is not in the same SNAP household. Cannot be double-counted with 273.9(d)(3)(x) medical attendant care.
key_quote: "Payments for dependent care when necessary for a household member to search for, accept or continue employment"

heading: Care provider/facility costs
summary: Costs of care given by an individual provider or care facility are deductible dependent-care expenses.

heading: Transportation to care
summary: Transportation costs to and from the care facility are deductible.

heading: Activity / fees for dependent care
summary: Activity or other fees associated with care provided to the dependent and necessary for household participation are deductible.

heading: Optional child support deduction (State option)
summary: State agency option: provide a deduction for legally obligated child support payments paid to or for a nonhousehold member (including arrears and vendor payments to third parties), in lieu of the 273.9(c)(17) exclusion. Alimony is not deductible under this option. STATE-OPTION JOIN.
key_quote: "At its option, the State agency may provide a deduction, rather than the income exclusion provided under paragraph (c)(17)"

heading: Shelter costs (umbrella)
summary: Three flavors of shelter relief: optional homeless shelter deduction, excess shelter deduction (capped except for elderly/disabled), and standard utility allowances.

heading: Homeless shelter deduction ($143)
summary: State agency option: provide a $143/month standard homeless shelter deduction to households where all members are homeless but not receiving free shelter throughout the month. May exclude households with extremely low shelter costs. STATE-OPTION JOIN.
key_quote: "A State agency may provide a standard homeless shelter deduction of $143 a month"

heading: Excess shelter deduction
summary: Monthly shelter expenses above 50% of post-other-deductions income are deductible, capped (for non-elderly/non-disabled households) at the maximum shelter deduction. Allowable expenses include rent/mortgage, property tax/insurance, utilities, internet, telephone, vacant-home costs, and repair costs from disasters.
key_quote: "Monthly shelter expenses in excess of 50 percent of the household income after all other deductions"

heading: Continuing shelter charges
summary: Rent, mortgage, condo/association fees, and other continuing ownership charges (including loan repayments and interest for mobile-home purchase) are allowable shelter expenses.

heading: Property taxes, assessments, structure insurance
summary: Property taxes, state/local assessments, and insurance on the structure (not personal-belongings insurance) are allowable shelter expenses.

heading: Utilities, telephone, internet
summary: Heating, cooling, electricity, water, sewerage, well/septic install and maintenance, garbage/trash, one telephone (all service fees), basic internet (monthly fees, taxes, one modem rental), and utility install fees are allowable. One-time deposits are not.

heading: Vacant-home shelter costs
summary: Shelter costs for a home temporarily unoccupied due to employment, training, illness, or disaster abandonment are deductible if the household intends to return, the home is not leased/rented during absence, and current occupants are not claiming the costs.

heading: Disaster repair costs
summary: Charges for repair of a home substantially damaged or destroyed by natural disaster are deductible -- but not if reimbursed by insurance, relief agencies, or other sources.

heading: Standard utility allowances
summary: State agencies may use standard utility allowances (SUAs) in place of actual costs. Allowable standards include: individual standards per utility, a heating/cooling-inclusive standard (HCSUA), and a limited utility allowance (LUA). Subject to State-Plan election, FNS methodology approval, and annual update. STATE-OPTION JOIN.

heading: Allowable SUA types
summary: States may use an individual-utility standard, a heating/cooling SUA (HCSUA), and an LUA. The LUA must cover at least two utilities and may include phone and/or internet. Same expense cannot be double-counted.

heading: Annual SUA review
summary: State agencies must review SUA amounts annually, round to the nearest whole dollar, and submit methodologies to FNS for approval when developed or changed.

heading: Five-year SUA methodology review
summary: State agencies must submit SUA methodologies to FNS at least every five years; baseline data and methodology must reflect recent trends, source data from utility providers, reflect low-income expenses, distinguish heating/cooling, and reflect residential utility expenses.

heading: HCSUA eligibility -- three pathways
summary: Heating/cooling SUA must be made available to households that pay heating/cooling separately, are billed individually by landlords or charged flat-rate, OR received a qualifying LIHEAP/similar payment greater than $20 annually in the current or preceding 12 months.
key_quote: "Households that receive a payment ... under the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Act of 1981 (LIHEAA) or other similar energy assistance program"

heading: HCSUA -- household incurs heating/cooling separately
summary: A household that incurs heating or cooling expenses separately from rent or mortgage is entitled to the HCSUA.

heading: HCSUA -- rentals billed individually or flat-rate
summary: Households in rental housing billed by landlords by individual usage or charged a flat rate separately from rent are entitled to the HCSUA. Public-housing excess-usage charges only qualify if the State mandates SUA use.

heading: HCSUA -- LIHEAP recipient ($20+/yr)
summary: Households that received (or had received on their behalf) a LIHEAP or similar payment greater than $20 annually in the current or preceding 12 months are entitled to the HCSUA.

heading: One SUA per household (occupied + unoccupied)
summary: A household with both an occupied home and an unoccupied home is entitled to only one SUA.

heading: Household choice between SUA and actual costs
summary: At initial certification, recertification, or move, the household may choose between an SUA and verified actual costs -- unless the State has mandated SUA use. 24-month-certified households may also switch at mandatory interim contact under 273.10(f)(1). STATE-OPTION JOIN.
key_quote: "the household may choose between a standard or verified actual utility costs"

heading: Mandatory SUA at State option
summary: State agency option: mandate use of SUAs for all households with qualifying expenses, provided the State has at least one heating/cooling and one non-heating/cooling SUA and the standards do not increase program costs (except for legitimate cost increases). STATE-OPTION JOIN.
key_quote: "A State agency may mandate use of standard utility allowances for all households"

heading: Proration of SUA in shared-housing situations
summary: If a household shares heating/cooling expenses with another individual or household, the State must not prorate the SUA where mandatory SUA use is in effect, and must not prorate if non-SNAP cohabitants are ineligible-only.

heading: Determining household eligibility and benefit levels
summary: Top-level section governing how the State agency determines eligibility, benefit levels, certification periods, and the mechanics of anticipating income/expenses across a certification period.

heading: Month of application (umbrella)
summary: Determines how eligibility, prorated benefits, and recertification work in the initial month and how anticipated changes affect allotments.

heading: Initial-month eligibility and benefit level
summary: Eligibility for the month of application is determined using the household's entire-month circumstances; benefit level is prorated from date of application to end of month (with special handling for institutional release and SSI joint applicants).

heading: Whole-month eligibility determination
summary: Eligibility for the month of application is determined by considering the household's circumstances for the entire calendar month (or, with FNS approval, a fiscal month).
key_quote: "determined for the month of application by considering the household circumstances for the entire month"

heading: Proration of initial-month benefits
summary: Initial-month benefits run from date of application to end of month; the State must prorate using either a standard 30-day month (treating the 31st as the 30th) or the exact length of the calendar/fiscal month. Initial month is defined here.
key_quote: "benefit level for the initial months of certification shall be based on the day of the month it applies for benefits"

heading: Proration formula and minimum issuance
summary: States use FNS proration tables or specified formulas; rounding produces whole-dollar allotments. If the prorated allotment is under $10 in the initial month, no issuance is made.
key_quote: "If the computation results in an allotment of less than $10, then no issuance shall be made for the initial month."

heading: Application for recertification
summary: Recertification eligibility is determined based on anticipated circumstances for the next certification period. Late recertification applications are treated as initial applications and prorated; a State-agency error means restoration of benefits per 273.14(e).

heading: Anticipated changes affecting eligibility month-to-month
summary: A household may be eligible in the month of application but ineligible in the next month (or vice versa) due to anticipated changes. The application is used for both months; if eligibility shifts, no reapplication is required.

heading: Variable allotments within a certification period
summary: Allotments may vary month-to-month within a certification period to reflect anticipated changes, unless the household elects to average per 273.10(c)(3) and (d)(3). Certification periods should be set to the longest period over which changes can be reasonably anticipated.
key_quote: "shall vary month to month within the certification period to reflect changes anticipated at the time of certification"

heading: Determining resources
summary: Available resources at the time of interview are used to determine eligibility.

heading: Determining income (umbrella)
summary: Three subsections govern how income is determined: anticipation, month-of-receipt counting, and averaging.

heading: Anticipating income
summary: Income already received during the certification period plus any reasonably-certain anticipated income is counted. Uncertain income (amount or timing) is not counted; in fluctuating cases the household may elect to average. This is the central rule for handling unstable gig/self-employment income.
household_types_affected: gig/contract workers, self-employed (non-farm), self-employed (farm), tipped workers, cash-paid workers
key_quote: "income already received by the household during the certification period and any anticipated income the household and the State agency are reasonably certain will be received"

heading: Standard for reasonable certainty
summary: If the amount or timing of income is uncertain, the uncertain portion is not counted. For new income sources (new job, recently applied PA), money is not anticipated unless there is reasonable certainty of month and amount. In fluctuating-but-certain cases the household may elect to income-average.
key_quote: "that portion of the household income that is uncertain shall not be counted by the State agency"

heading: 30-day past income as indicator; seasonal/fluctuating exceptions
summary: Income received in the past 30 days is the default indicator of anticipated income, but past income is not used when changes have occurred or can be anticipated. A longer past period may be used for fluctuating income, and the most recent comparable season for seasonal income.
household_types_affected: self-employed (farm), gig/contract workers, tipped workers, cash-paid workers
key_quote: "Income received during the past 30 days shall be used as an indicator of the income that is and will be available to the household"

heading: Income counted only in month received (or averaged)
summary: Anticipated income counts only in the month it is expected to be received unless averaged. Weekly-to-monthly conversion uses x4.3, biweekly uses x2.15 (or the State PA conversion standard or exact monthly figure). Nonrecurring lump sums are not income.
key_quote: "convert the income to a monthly amount by multiplying weekly amounts by 4.3 and biweekly amounts by 2.15"

heading: Conversion of weekly / biweekly income
summary: Weekly-to-monthly conversion uses x4.3; biweekly uses x2.15. State PA conversion standards or the exact monthly figure can be used as alternatives.

heading: Held wages, employer-held wages, wage advances
summary: Wages held at employee request count in the month they would otherwise have been paid. Wages held by the employer as general practice are NOT counted until paid out. Wage advances count in the month received only if reasonably anticipated.
household_types_affected: all earned-income households, tipped workers, cash-paid workers

heading: Mailing/pay-date timing variations
summary: Recurring monthly or semimonthly income shall not be varied month-to-month merely because of mailing-cycle shifts or pay-date weekends/holidays.

heading: Income averaging
summary: States may apply income averaging statewide for categories of households, recalculating at recertification and after reported income changes. Conversion of weekly/biweekly income does not constitute averaging. STATE METHODOLOGY JOIN.
key_quote: "Income may be averaged in accordance with methods established by the State agency to be applied Statewide for categories of households"

heading: Statewide-category averaging methodology
summary: The State agency establishes the averaging methodology, applied statewide for defined categories, using the household's own anticipation of monthly income fluctuations. Recalculated at recertification and on reported changes.

heading: 12-month averaging for contract / self-employment income
summary: Households that derive annual income in a period shorter than 1 year by contract or self-employment (e.g., school employees, sharecroppers, farmers) must have that income averaged over 12 months, unless paid hourly or by piecework. Does not apply to migrant/seasonal farmworkers. Self-employment averaging procedures are in 273.11.
key_quote: "Households which, by contract or self-employment, derive their annual income in a period of time shorter than 1 year shall have that income averaged over a 12-month period"

heading: Educational-income averaging
summary: Earned and unearned educational income (after exclusions) is averaged over the period the income is intended to cover. Income may be counted in the month received or anticipated for first installment, but is prorated over the intended period.

heading: Determining deductions (umbrella)
summary: Sets out how deductions are applied: disallowed expenses, when expenses are deductible (month billed), averaging, anticipation, conversion, energy assistance, SSI medical deduction, and the optional child support deduction.

heading: Disallowed expenses (umbrella)
summary: Expenses covered by excluded income (education, vendor payments, demonstration cash conversions, JOBS/TCC reimbursements, HUD utility reimbursements) and expenses paid by other household members or in-kind are not deductible.

heading: Expenses covered by excluded income -- disallowed
summary: Expenses covered by excluded educational assistance, excluded vendor payments (including demonstration cash conversions), JOBS/TCC dependent-care reimbursements, and HUD/FmHA utility reimbursements are not deductible. Nonreimbursable portions of medical expenses remain deductible.

heading: Expenses paid in-kind or by another household member -- disallowed
summary: Deductions only apply when the service is provided by someone outside the household and the household makes a money payment. In-kind compensation and intra-household care are not deductible.
key_quote: "Expenses shall only be deductible if the service is provided by someone outside of the household and the household makes a money payment for the service."

heading: Billed expenses (month-of-bill rule)
summary: An expense is deductible only in the month it is billed or becomes due, regardless of when paid. Amounts carried forward from past billing periods are not deductible. A particular expense may only be deducted once.
key_quote: "a deduction shall be allowed only in the month the expense is billed or otherwise becomes due"

heading: Averaging expenses (household election)
summary: Households may elect to average fluctuating expenses, expenses billed less often than monthly (over the interval), or one-time expenses across the certification period. Special rules apply to one-time medical expenses for 24-month certifications.
key_quote: "Households may elect to have fluctuating expenses averaged."

heading: Anticipating expenses
summary: Expenses are based on what the household expects to be billed during the certification period. The most recent month's bills are the default basis. Past expenses must not be averaged as a forecast for SUA-less utility cases. Medical expenses must be reported and verified at certification.
key_quote: "The State agency shall calculate a household expenses based on the expenses the household expects to be billed for during the certification period."

heading: Conversion of deductions
summary: Income-conversion procedures (x4.3 weekly, x2.15 biweekly) also apply to expenses billed weekly or biweekly.

heading: Proration of energy assistance payments
summary: Energy assistance payments are prorated over the entire heating or cooling season they are intended to cover. Prorated payments may qualify the household for HCSUA in more than one season.

heading: SSI-recipient medical and uncapped shelter deductions on retroactive period
summary: Households with a disabled SSI member are entitled to the excess medical deduction (273.9(d)(3)) and the uncapped excess shelter deduction (273.9(d)(5)) back to the SSI authorization date or SNAP application date, whichever is later -- including in restored-benefit cases.

heading: Optional child support deduction -- budgeting
summary: If the State has elected the 273.9(d)(5) deduction, it may budget child support per 273.10(d)(2)-(5) or retrospectively under 273.21, regardless of how other circumstances are budgeted. STATE-OPTION JOIN.

heading: Calculating net income and benefit levels (umbrella)
summary: The step-by-step computation of net income, the eligibility tests, the allotment formula, destitute household rules, and the Thrifty Food Plan / maximum allotment basis.

heading: Net monthly income calculation (umbrella)
summary: Specifies the ordered eight-step net-income computation and the rounding-procedure options.

heading: Eight-step net-income computation
summary: Net income is computed by: (A) adding gross earned + unearned income, (B) subtracting 20% earned income deduction, (C) subtracting standard deduction, (D) subtracting medical excess, (E) subtracting dependent care, (F) subtracting child-support deduction if elected, (G) subtracting homeless shelter deduction, (H) computing excess shelter (shelter minus 50% of net), and (I) subtracting capped excess shelter (uncapped for elderly/disabled).
key_quote: "To determine a household net monthly income"

heading: Step 1: gross income, with farm self-employment loss offset
summary: Sum gross monthly earned plus unearned income, minus exclusions. Self-employment farm losses are offset per 273.11(a)(2)(iii).
key_quote: "Net losses from the self-employment income of a farmer shall be offset in accordance with 273.11(a)(2)(iii)."

heading: Step 2: 20% earned income deduction
summary: Multiply gross earned income by 20% and subtract; or multiply by 80% and add back to unearned. Excluded earnings used to pay excluded child support are still multiplied by 20% and subtracted.
key_quote: "Multiply the total gross monthly earned income by 20 percent and subtract that amount from the total gross income"

heading: Step 3: subtract standard deduction
summary: Subtract the standard deduction (273.9(d)(1)).

heading: Step 4: subtract excess medical (elderly/disabled only)
summary: If entitled to excess medical deduction (273.9(d)(3)) and total medical exceeds $35, subtract the portion above $35.

heading: Step 5: subtract dependent care
summary: Subtract allowable monthly dependent-care expenses per 273.9(d)(4) for each dependent.

heading: Step 6: subtract child support deduction (if elected)
summary: If the State has elected child support as a deduction rather than an exclusion, subtract allowable monthly child support per 273.9(d)(5). STATE-OPTION JOIN.

heading: Step 7: subtract homeless shelter deduction (if any)
summary: Subtract the homeless shelter deduction (up to $143) if applicable; bars further shelter computation under (H).

heading: Step 8a: compute excess shelter (50% of income test)
summary: Total allowable shelter expenses; subtract 50% of post-deduction monthly income. Remainder is excess shelter cost.
key_quote: "Subtract from total shelter costs 50 percent of the household monthly income after all the above deductions"

heading: Step 8b: subtract excess shelter (capped or uncapped)
summary: Subtract excess shelter cost from post-deduction income -- capped for non-elderly/non-disabled households at the maximum shelter deduction; uncapped for households with an elderly or disabled member.
key_quote: "Households not subject to a capped shelter expense shall have the full amount exceeding 50 percent of their net income subtracted."

heading: Rounding procedure options
summary: State agency must use one of two rounding procedures: (A) round 1-49 cents down, 50-99 cents up; or (B) apply the State's TANF-program rounding. The State may carry cents through individual shelter and medical costs and round only the final deduction. STATE-OPTION JOIN.

heading: Eligibility and benefits (umbrella)
summary: Compares net income to standards, treats students-aging-out, and prescribes the allotment formula and minimum benefits.

heading: Elderly/disabled net-only income test
summary: Households with an elderly or disabled member have net income compared to the 273.9(a)(2) monthly net income standard.

heading: Non-elderly/disabled gross + net income tests
summary: Households without an elderly or disabled member must additionally pass the gross income test under 273.9(a)(1).

heading: Destitute household eligibility under 273.10(e)(3)
summary: Destitute households (migrant/seasonal farmworkers) have their gross and net income computed under 273.10(e)(3) and compared to the appropriate standard.

heading: 59-turning-60 elderly status during month of application
summary: If a household member turns 60 during the month of application, the State must use the elderly-eligibility test under (e)(2)(i)(A).

heading: Student turning 18 during certification
summary: If a student whose income is excluded under 273.9(c)(7) turns 18 during the month of application, the State excludes the earnings in the month of application and counts them the following month. If turning 18 mid-certification, exclusion continues through the month they turn 18.

heading: Allotment formula: TFP minus 30% of net
summary: The monthly allotment equals the maximum SNAP allotment for the household's size, reduced by 30% of net monthly income. Rounding: either round 30%-of-net up to the nearest dollar, or do not round 30%-of-net and round the final allotment down.
key_quote: "household monthly allotment shall be equal to the maximum SNAP allotment for the household size reduced by 30 percent of the household net monthly income"

heading: Initial-month minimum-issuance threshold
summary: If the initial-month calculation yields less than $10, no benefits are issued for the initial month.
key_quote: "If the calculation of benefits ... for an initial month would yield an allotment of less than $10 ... no benefits shall be issued"

heading: Minimum benefit for 1- and 2-person households
summary: After the initial month, all eligible one- and two-person households receive a minimum monthly allotment of 8% of the maximum allotment for a household of one, rounded to the nearest dollar.
key_quote: "all eligible one-person and two-person households shall receive minimum monthly allotments equal to the minimum benefit"

heading: No-benefit households of 3+ -- denial or suspension
summary: Eligible 3+-person households entitled to no benefits may be denied or suspended at State option. Suspended households retain reapplication rights and a conversion-to-issuance procedure on change reporting. STATE-OPTION JOIN.

heading: Initial-month no-benefit handling
summary: Households entitled to no benefits in their initial month but entitled in subsequent months are certified beginning with the month of application.

heading: Mid-certification standard changes
summary: When circumstances change such that a different income standard applies, the State applies it at the next recertification or whenever it changes eligibility/benefit level/certification period -- whichever is first.

heading: Reductions / suspensions / cancellations of allotments
summary: Procedures for benefit reductions, suspensions, or cancellations ordered under 271.7, including treatment of minimum benefits during 90%+ reductions.

heading: Destitute households
summary: Migrant/seasonal farmworker households with little/no income but with prior or new income in the application month qualify for destitute treatment -- expedited service and special income calculation that disregards anticipated new-source income after the application date. Non-migrant/seasonal households cannot be destitute.
key_quote: "Migrant or seasonal farmworker households may have little or no income at the time of application and may be in need of immediate food assistance"

heading: Destitute -- terminated-source income
summary: Households whose only application-month income was received prior to application and is from a terminated source are destitute and receive expedited service. (A) Monthly-or-more-frequent income is terminated if not received again in the balance of the application month or the next month. (B) Less-frequent income terminates if not received in the next normal payment month.

heading: Destitute -- new-source income (>$25 by day 10)
summary: Households whose only application-month income is from a new source are destitute if income above $25 from that new source will not be received by the 10th calendar day after application. New-source thresholds differ for monthly+ and less-frequent income.

heading: Destitute -- combined terminated + new source
summary: Households may receive both terminated-source pre-application income and new-source post-application income and still be destitute if no other income is received in the application month and new-source income above $25 will not arrive by day 10.

heading: Destitute calculation -- disregard post-application new income
summary: Destitute eligibility and benefits are calculated using only income received between the first of the month and the date of application. Anticipated new-source post-application income is disregarded.
key_quote: "Any income from a new source that is anticipated after the day of application shall be disregarded."

heading: Destitute treatment of employer travel advances
summary: Travel advances from a new employer are excluded as reimbursements (and do not affect destitute determination) unless by written contract they are wage advances subtracted from later wages, in which case they count as income but still do not affect the destitute determination.

heading: Same employer / migrant crew-chief rule
summary: A member changing jobs but staying with the same employer is treated as still receiving income from the same source. A migrant farmworker's source is the grower, not the crew chief -- moving growers means moving sources.

heading: Destitute treatment at recertification
summary: Destitute procedures apply at initial application and recertification, but only for the first month of each certification period.

heading: Thrifty Food Plan (TFP) and maximum allotments
summary: Maximum allotments are based on the TFP, uniform by household size in the 48 contiguous states/DC. TFPs are adjusted annually and posted by FNS. Hawaii, Alaska, Guam, and USVI TFPs are computed with geographic price adjustments.

heading: Maximum SNAP allotment level -- TFP-based
summary: Maximum allotments are based on the TFP and uniform across the 48 contiguous states/DC. Separate Hawaii, Alaska, Guam, USVI TFPs reflect local food price adjustments. Posted annually by FNS.
key_quote: "Maximum SNAP allotments shall be based on the TFP"

heading: Annual TFP-based adjustment
summary: Effective Oct. 1, 1996, maximum SNAP allotments must be based on 100% of the cost of the TFP for the preceding June, rounded to the nearest lower dollar -- with a floor that allotments not fall below those in effect on September 30, 1996.

heading: Certification periods (umbrella)
summary: Sets out certification-period length rules: must be definite, no longer than 12 months (24 for elderly/disabled or reservation households on monthly reporting), with rules for shortening and lengthening.

heading: 24-month certification for all-elderly/disabled households
summary: Households where all adult members are elderly or disabled may be certified for up to 24 months. The State must contact the household at least once every 12 months by any method it chooses.
key_quote: "may certify for up to 24 months households in which all adult members are elderly or disabled"

heading: 24-month certification for reservation households on monthly reporting
summary: Households residing on a reservation that the State requires to submit monthly reports under 273.21 are certified for 24 months unless FNS waives the requirement.

heading: Certification period length guidance
summary: States should assign the longest certification period consistent with circumstances; at least 6 months unless unstable or ABAWD-containing; 3-month floor for unstable/ABAWD; 1-2 months for households likely to become ineligible soon.

heading: 6-month minimum certification period
summary: Households should be assigned certification periods of at least 6 months, unless circumstances are unstable or the household contains an ABAWD.

heading: Unstable / ABAWD: 3-month minimum
summary: Households with unstable circumstances (e.g., zero net income) or with an ABAWD member should be assigned certification periods consistent with their circumstances, generally no less than 3 months.
household_types_affected: gig/contract workers, tipped workers, cash-paid workers, all earned-income households
key_quote: "Households with unstable circumstances ... and households with an ABAWD member should be assigned certification periods consistent with their circumstances, but generally no less than 3 months."

heading: 1- to 2-month certification when ineligibility likely
summary: 1- or 2-month certification periods may be assigned when it appears likely the household will become ineligible in the near future.

heading: Shortening certification periods
summary: The State may not end a certification period earlier than its assigned termination date except for ineligibility, 273.12(c)(3) noncompliance, or to comply with 273.12(a)(5). Loss of PA or employment status changes alone are insufficient.

heading: Lengthening certification periods
summary: States may extend a certification period once established, capped at 24 months for elderly/disabled households or 12 months for others, and must notify the household.

heading: Certification notices to households (umbrella)
summary: Sets out required written notices for initial applications and recertifications, including notice of eligibility, denial, and pending status.

heading: Initial-application notices
summary: States must provide applicants with notice of eligibility, denial, or pending status as soon as a determination is made -- no later than 30 days after initial application.

heading: Notice of eligibility content requirements
summary: Notice of eligibility must specify the allotment amount, certification period dates, anticipated variations, fair-hearing rights, SNAP office contact, and (where available) free legal-representation resources.

heading: Notice of denial
summary: Notice of denial explains the basis for denial, fair-hearing rights, SNAP office contact, and legal representation. Categorically-eligible-pending households must be asked to report subsequent PA/SSI/GA approvals.

heading: Notice of pending status
summary: If the application is held pending due to State action or household action needed, the State must inform the household in writing of pending status and any further required action, with the 60-day denial deadline.

heading: Recertification notices
summary: Households filing recertification by the 15th of the last certification month must receive eligibility/denial notice by end of period; those with notice-of-expiration get a notice no later than 30 days after the last allotment opportunity.
